g.text: SCP is not a full transitive reduction: X1 → D4 (amber) is still implied by X1 → X2 → B2 → B3 → D3 → D4, because it is the only (hence latest) candidate in S[N1]. In a 1835-plan random test,

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: 15% of SCP graphs kept at least one such edge. Harmless for correctness; it only means 'at most one type-2 edge per action', not 'minimal'.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The ADG after both improvements: no waits, at most one type-2 edge per action

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Type-2 edges: 15 in the original ADG (figure 2.4) → 12 after dropping the two waits (CP finds exactly these) → 8 with SCP. Red dashed: the 4 edges SCP skips;

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: each is implied by a path of solid edges.
